To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in Italy the total annual cost for the prevention of cervical cancer is approximately €181,500,000, of which 86.9% is attributable to Pap smears.
cervical cancer screening in Italy costs €181.5M/year, and that screening accounts for 87% of total costs.
in Italy, the number of women screened annually is 6.4 millions, of which 1.2 and 5.3 million are screened through organized and opportunitic screening programs, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an epidemiological and economic model for cervical cancer screening in Italy.
the development and validation of the Italian version of the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer (EORTC) quality of life questionnaire (QLQ-C30).
the development of an epidemiological model of cervical cancer in Italy and the estimation of the costs of cervical screening and management of cervical abnormalities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cost of screening for cervical cancer and management of cervical abnormalities in Italy amounts to €181.5 (95% CI: 181.1–181.9) million annually.
the costs of cervical cancer prevention are not excessive in Italy.
cervical cancer screening and follow-up in Italy are associated with substantial direct costs to the health system, but the cost of screening per case of CIN2+ detected is relatively low.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the total cost for cervical cancer prevention in 2009 in Italy was approximately €181.6 million (€158.5 million and €22.8 million for screening and for management of cervical abnormalities, respectively).
cervical cancer prevention in women aged 25 to 69 years in Italy costs approximately €181 million per year.
cervical cancer screening and management of cervical abnormalities are associated with a substantial cost to the healthcare system in Italy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the total annual cost is relatively low compared with that of other cancers.
the cost of screening is high, even in the absence of organized screening programs, and that the cost of management of cervical abnormalities is not trivial.
cervical cancer is a very costly condition and the cost of its prevention is high.
